subject: Control mapping & regression plan for EU AI Act + NIST review
content:
From: Anna Müller <anna.muller@healthcorp.de>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 08:24:00 +0100
Subject: Request: mapping to EU AI Act + NIST and regression / eval plan

Hi Soojin,

We're running through our final supplier security review for the AI components in our patient triage product. Two asks from Security & Procurement: a mapping of Redwood's controls to the EU AI Act (high-risk obligations) and NIST AI RMF categories, and a short description of your regression/eval approach we can include as part of our technical due diligence.

Specifically we need:
- A control matrix that shows which technical/organizational controls map to Article 10/11 obligations (transparency, risk management, record-keeping, Cx audits) and the NIST functions (Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Recover).
- A description of how you run quality/regression checks when model versions change (test suites, metrics, canarying, rollback criteria).
- Any evidence artifacts (SOC 2 index, change logs, regression report template).

Ideal timeline: if possible we'd like a draft by next Tuesday (16 Mar) so our legal/security teams can review ahead of our supplier board on 22 Mar. Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Anna Müller
Head of Security Engineering
HealthCorp GmbH

---
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Müller <anna.muller@healthcorp.de>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: mapping to EU AI Act + NIST and regression / eval plan

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear asks. We can provide the control mapping and an operational summary of our regression approach.

Quick notes:
- Target: draft control matrix + regression outline to you by Mon 15 Mar (so you have Tue for internal prep).
- Evidence: we'll attach a SOC 2 artifacts index and a regression harness outline; note some SOC 2 items require an NDA/portal access — happy to provide the index and coordinate access.
- For the regression writeup we'll cover: evaluation datasets, metric suite (accuracy, hallucination rate proxy, token-level latency), canary-ing strategy, automated regression harness, and rollback triggers.

Looping in Karthik and Neha for the mapping and artifacts. Marcus — if you can compile the SOC 2 artifact index and any recent regression reports, please do.

Would you like a short walkthrough call after we send the draft? We can do 30 minutes.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft control mapping (internal)

Soojin / Neha — attaching my first-pass mapping. High-level summary below; workbook attached as control_mapping_eu_nist.xlsx.

Summary:
- EU AI Act: We marked obligations across Articles 5, 10, 13, 14 where applicable for our hosted API (data minimization, transparency, human oversight, documentation, risk management). For "high-risk" classification items (model documentation, technical mitigation), we included the relevant runtime features (explainability hooks, system prompts, function-calling controls).
- NIST AI RMF: Controls are mapped to Identify (model inventory, versioning), Protect (access controls, KMS), Detect (anomaly monitoring for latency/inference drift), Respond/Recover (automatic fallback to model variant, incident runbooks).
- Gaps: audit log retention for customer-managed private deployments needs explicit configuration guidance (we flagged as action item).

Attachments: control_mapping_eu_nist.xlsx (includes column for customer evidence and maturity level).

Notes for the regression section (outline):
1) Eval harness: deterministic prompt suites, randomized adversarial prompts, domain-specific holdout sets.
2) Metrics: top-line pass/fail (regression gate), AUROC on intent classifiers, semantic similarity thresholds, hallucination sentinel checks.
3) Canarying: 1% traffic for 48 hours, synthetic prompt injection, compare KPIs vs baseline.
4) Rollback criteria: delta>5% in critical metric (safety/accuracy) or error rate spike.

Can Neha and Marcus add the artifact list (SOC 2 pointers) and an example regression report? I can fold this into the matrix and produce the customer-facing workbook.

—Karthik

Attachment: [Attachment: control_mapping_eu_nist.xlsx (xlsx)]

---
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft control mapping (internal)

Thanks Karthik — this is a good structure. A few items I'll add before we send to HealthCorp:
- Regression artifacts: include an example post-deployment regression report (regression_harness_outline.pdf) and a short FAQ on canary design choices.
- Eval details: show sample prompts and expected outputs, plus tooling (we use an internal harness that runs nightly against pinned prompt suites).
- Data lineage: clarify that customer data is not retained beyond configured retention windows and that Private deployments can opt-in to on-prem artifact storage.
- Evidence access: SOC 2 artifacts index will be a text manifest (soc2_artifacts_index.txt) with instructions to request a read-only link.

I'll prep the FAQ and example report, and then Karthik can integrate into the workbook.

-Neha

Attachment: [Attachment: regression_harness_outline.pdf (pdf)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Müller <anna.muller@healthcorp.de>, procurement@healthcorp.de
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: mapping to EU AI Act + NIST and regression / eval plan

Anna — attaching the draft deliverables for your review.

What's attached:
- control_mapping_eu_nist.xlsx — control matrix with EU AI Act articles mapped to Redwood controls, NIST functions, evidence column with suggested artifacts.
- regression_harness_outline.pdf — an operational summary of our regression and evaluation approach, including canarying, metrics, and rollback triggers.
- soc2_artifacts_index.txt — index of SOC 2 artifacts and instructions for requesting secure access.

Highlights / quick answers to your asks:
- Mapping: We map our runtime features and organizational processes to EU AI Act obligations (documentation, transparency, risk management) and to NIST RMF functions. The workbook includes maturity notes for hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options.
- Regression / eval: We run nightly deterministic and adversarial suites against pinned prompt sets; candidate model versions must pass an automated regression gate (critical safety/accuracy metrics) before canarying. Canarying runs at 1–2% of traffic for 24–72 hours with synthetic probes; rollback is automatic if critical metrics regress beyond configured thresholds.
- Evidence: SOC 2 index points to encryption, change control, and monitoring artifacts. For details that require NDAs or portal access (full reports), we can provide read-only links.

Next steps we propose:
1) Please review the workbook and outline and mark any gaps by EOD Thu 18 Mar.
2) Let's schedule a 30-minute walkthrough the week of 22 Mar (we're available Tue/Wed morning CET).
3) If needed, we can produce a short red-team summary and additional fairness bias checks tailored to your clinical prompts.

If this looks good, I'll send the links to the secure artifact portal and set up the call.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: [control_mapping_eu_nist.xlsx], [regression_harness_outline.pdf], [soc2_artifacts_index.txt]
